concepts.name: Newton's laws in brief
concepts.source_span: Newton's Laws of Motion are three fundamental laws that explain the relationship between the motion of an object and the forces acting on it.

questions.stem: How many fundamental laws of motion did Newton introduce?
What do Newton's Laws of Motion explain?
options: The relationship between the motion of an object and the forces acting on it
How electricity moves in a wire

questions.stem: Newton's laws form the foundation of which area of physics?
Who introduced the three laws of motion?
Which of these is NOT one of Newton's three laws?

concepts.name: The first law: inertia
concepts.source_span: An object remains at rest or continues moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.

questions.stem: What does the first law say about an object at rest?
options: It starts moving on its own
It remains at rest unless an unbalanced external force acts on it

questions.stem: What is inertia?
options: The force that pulls objects towards the Earth
The speed of a moving object
The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of rest or motion
The energy stored in a spring

questions.stem: Why do passengers move forward when a moving bus suddenly stops?
options: Their bodies tend to continue moving because of inertia

questions.stem: A book placed on a table stays at rest until:
options: Someone applies a force to move it

concepts.name: The second law: F = ma
concepts.source_span: The acceleration of an object depends on the net force applied and its mass.

questions.stem: Which formula expresses the second law of motion?
What happens to acceleration when the applied force increases and the mass stays the same?
What happens to acceleration when the mass increases and the force stays the same?
In F = ma, in which unit is force measured?
Why is an empty shopping cart easier to push than a fully loaded one?
options: Gravity pulls less on the handle
It has less mass, so the same force gives it more acceleration

concepts.name: The third law: action and reaction
concepts.source_span: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.stem: According to the third law, when one object applies a force on another, the second object:
options: Applies an equal force in the opposite direction
Applies a larger force in the same direction
Applies a smaller force in the opposite direction

questions.stem: When we walk, what pushes us forward?
options: The ground pushing us forward as our feet push it backwards

questions.stem: How does a rocket move upward?
options: By pulling on the air above it
By using the Earth's magnetic field

questions.stem: How does a swimmer move forward?
options: By lifting their body out of the water
